image_description: The image displays three mallard ducks on a wet, paved surface. The primary subject is a male mallard (drake) in the foreground, standing and facing right, showing distinct breeding plumage with an iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey body. A second drake stands slightly behind it to the right. In the background left, a female mallard (hen) with mottled brown plumage is visible, partially out of focus. The setting appears to be an urban or park environment with wet ground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground drake clearly exhibits a broad, flat, yellow-green bill characteristic of a mallard drake. The shape and color match the taxonomy description perfectly.
The eye of the foreground drake is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is stocky and compact. The plumage appears dense and well-defined, typical of waterfowl.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground subject displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey flanks. This matches the 'mallard' specific description in the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The orange legs are visible on the foreground drake. They are positioned towards the rear of the body. The feet are clearly webbed with the correct anatomical structure (palmate).
The wings are folded against the body but show the characteristic broad shape and pointed tips of duck wings. The speculum (blue/purple patch with white borders) is visible on the foreground drake.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short. On the foreground drake, the central tail feathers are visibly curled upward, a key sexual dimorphism trait for mallard drakes.
